terra.problem: The flour joke compares the scattering of Israel to a mishap on the counter, making light of people’s suffering.
Not everything listed afterward is about what was done to the people or the land. The LORD also says His silver, gold, and treasures were taken to their temples.
The Greeks are the people to whom Judah and Jerusalem were sold. The verse does not name the place where they were sent.
The nations are called to come quickly and advance, but the text does not say they actually rush to the valley.
“I'll leave it at what the text says” comments on how Papa tells the passage.
The verse says there are multitudes in the valley; it does not say the crowds are still gathering or give that as the reason the Day is near.
“I'm only telling you what the verse says” comments on how Papa tells the passage.
“I'll just leave it at that” comments on how Papa tells the passage.
The verse says the LORD roars from Zion and is a refuge for His people. It does not say whether He is watching from a distance.
“Quite the opposite” implies that His people can hear His voice. The verse says He raises His voice, but does not say who hears it.
The loophole joke makes the wording of the LORD's promise the subject of humor.
The plumbing joke makes the spring flowing from the LORD's house the subject of humor.
